title: Dispatch independent contributions concurrently and react to coordination events
goal: Make the full W3 team operate around criteria and work boundaries: useful independent work can overlap while notices, bids, leases and objections change subsequent admissions.
scope: Replace fixed W1 sequencing with agent proposals and complete solicitation/award at event-driven work boundaries. Wake on invocation, Board, offer deadline, lease and user action; do not starve stop behind unrelated writes. Apply authorized policy/parameter changes only at recorded boundaries, preserving exact effective selections for past decisions.

Schedule only dependency-independent WorkItems with compatible effective workspace access within parallel_limit, attempt_limit, max_members and Treasury constraints. Permit multiple Producer/Researcher assignments when safe; serialize interfering writes and dependent work.

Integrate agent-generated proposals, all P3 responses, objections, handoffs, diagnosis and team/profile changes into the same Dispatcher. Role completions produce the correct result/evidence/notice/review payloads rather than a generic “agent finished” fact.

Recover dynamic sessions from Journal: pending solicitations, committed awards, active/expired commitments and questions remain coherent after interruption. Provide one executable cooperation scenario showing actual reassignment/replanning/concurrent contribution and an audited result through the prerequisite projections/TUI.
acceptance: A deterministic real-filesystem scenario shows an agent initiating useful work not preallocated by the fixed workflow, offers changing allocation, transferred responsibility, and objections/status notices changing the plan. Independent contributions overlap; dependent/conflicting work waits; the audited report accounts for all calls.

Concurrent completion/board/expiry events cannot double-award a contribution, keep two active commitments for one assignment or admit work against a stale plan. A runtime restart preserves outstanding allocation and avoids repeating native starts.

The user can inspect why the team changed and which criterion/evidence gap each admitted contribution addresses. More messages or participants alone are never presented as measured quality or speed improvement.
context: Authority: ymp-docs/self-organizing-team-domain-model.md, A1/A3/A4/A5/A9, P1–P7, sections 3.3/3.5, principles 2/6/7/13 and R-3/R-12/R-17. Use the approved model with 811a872 semantics and the greenfield baseline in 0c61ff1 and §5.8 for experimental strategy boundaries. Other documents and existing names explain implementation facts only.

Greenfield: create this behavior in the new implementation. Paths below are PROPOSED target modules under the layout owned by W1-0001; only completed prerequisite tasks supply implementation. Prior source, APIs, fixtures and delivery claims are not a baseline.

Build dynamic scheduling in proposed runtime/dispatcher.rs using the W1 loop and completed W3 protocols. Permit real independent overlap without holding a global adapter lock across all work; kernel event commits still enforce concurrency and authority.

All P1–P6 mechanisms are prerequisite outputs, and P7 protects CheckDesigner/Board visibility. W4 adds competing attempt groups; W5 adds experience. User stop must not be starved and stops autonomous model work until applicable continuation.

The demonstration must show initiative, offers and transferred commitments changing admitted work and plan, not just simultaneous messages. Preserve each experiment’s implementation/parameter selection at authorized work boundaries and report costs/limitations honestly.

history.note: Plan new implementation from greenfield baseline 0c61ff1, preserving approved experimental mechanisms, reporting/evidence/recovery rules and explicit prerequisite boundaries.
